summary: Edge retry convergence overwrote per-request model pin during staged canary causing silent fallback to older quantized variant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NexaContent) reported degraded answer quality and unexpected higher latency spikes for a small subset of tenant requests during a staged canary for redwood/gptx-7b. They had explicitly pinned their routes to v2026-02-18.

Impact:
- ~0.6% of tenant requests during a 45-minute window were served by the older quantized variant (gptx-7b-quant) despite explicit per-request pin header. Resulted in truncated outputs and higher tokenization delta.
- Customer-grade downstream QA flagged content regressions; one production job retried and recorded higher billable token counts.

Environment:
- Production, us-east-1.
- Tenant on enterprise plan with model-version pin header present in requests (X-Model-Pin).

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer + reproduced in house):
1) Set route to pinned model v2026-02-18 via X-Model-Pin header.
2) Initiate traffic mix: 98% normal, 2% high-latency simulated (introduce artificial 250ms delay on one edge host).
3) Trigger the canary weight shift (10% -> 20%) via control-plane.
4) Observe retries from edge-proxy when backend health probes return 503 during the induced delay.

Observed behavior:
- When edge-proxy triggered a retry for in-flight requests, retry convergence logic reconstructed a route snapshot from the edge cache that lacked the per-request pin in the reconstructed metadata. The request retry was routed to an autoscaled prewarm pool that had only the quantized variant available, leading to silent fallback.
- Retry loop returned 200 but with quantized-model signatures in response headers.
- No explicit pin-override logs in control-plane; edge logs show retry path merged from 'edge-cache-snapshot-v2' which omits request-scoped pins under rare race conditions.

Expected behavior:
- Retries should preserve request-scoped pin headers and prefer the pinned variant or fail fast if pinned variant is unavailable. Edge-cache snapshots must include per-request pin attachments or instruct retries to re-fetch full routing metadata from the control-plane.

Logs / evidence:
- Excerpt from edge-proxy log (masked tenant): 
  [2026-03-01T09:22:11Z] request-id=rt-8a3c edge-host=eg-12 retry=1 original-pin=v2026-02-18 routed-model=redwood/gptx-7b-quant@v2025-12-04
- Tracing shows retry decision at edge-host eg-12 occurred 120ms after first attempt; prewarm pool candidate list did not include pinned model.
- Customer attached sample prompts and outputs (attached to ticket in secure S3 link).

Business/operational notes:
- Customer impact limited but visible in QA automation for NexaContent; they escalated due to content quality regressions.
- Potential billing discrepancy for retry-caused extra tokens.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis: edge-cache snapshot merging logic prunes transient request-scoped metadata when snapshot exceeds size threshold; retries reconstruct route using a compacted snapshot that intentionally omits ephemeral attachments. Under heavy canary churn + induced edge retry, that compaction hits a code path that does not re-apply explicit X-Model-Pin header.
- Confirmed via local reproduce: toggling EDGE_CACHE_COMPACT_THRESHOLD prevents omission.
- Control-plane did not record any pin-reconciles for affected requests (consistent with omission at edge).
- Orchestrator prewarm autoscale created nodes with only quantized model due to delayed model-pull for the fresh variant; when retry selected a prewarm candidate, fallback occurred.

Workaround (customer-facing):
- Short-term: Recommend NexaContent add a middleware to set a duplicate header X-Model-Pin-Static that our edge-proxy recognizes from the connection-level metadata (edge will not compact connection metadata currently). This preserves pin information across retries. Applied as temporary mitigation for affected tenant and saw no further quantized fallbacks in next 6h.
- Alternate: Increase canary prewarm pool capacity for the pinned variant temporarily to reduce chance of picking quantized-only candidates.

Next steps / engineering plan:
1) Add a quick fix to edge-proxy: ensure retry path re-fetches full routing metadata from control-plane when compacted edge snapshot lacks request-scoped pins (hotfix candidate).
2) Add unit/integration tests that simulate cache compaction + retries preserving per-request pins.
3) Adjust default cache compaction policy to never evict request-scoped pin attachments for enterprise-tier tenants.
4) Longer-term: Add observability metric for 'retry-preserved-pin' ratio and alert if below 99.9%.

Customer communication plan:
- CS (assigned) to send interim mitigation summary to NexaContent within 2 hours of ticket assignment (done). Engineering to provide ETA for hotfix within 24 hours.

2026-03-01 13:30 - Edge Eng (Marco): Reproduced locally by simulating edge host delay. Observed compaction path dropping X-Model-Pin. Drafted a short repro branch. Marking as P1 due to enterprise customer impact.

2026-03-02 09:17 - Orchestrator Eng (Sofia): Confirmed prewarm pool creation timing allowed quantized-only nodes to be selected. Adding commit to ensure prewarm includes pinned variants when a pin header is observed in traffic snapshot.

2026-03-03 08:55 - Marco: Preparing hotfix PR and will run canary for the patch in staging. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/2412. Planning to coordinate a short maintenance window for prod patch roll-forward if staging looks good.
investigation_notes: Edge cache compaction logic is the leading cause: compaction removes ephemeral request attachments. Retry reconstruction reuses compacted snapshot without consulting request headers when snapshot timestamp is within 'freshness' window. Repro branch adds explicit copy of request-scoped pins into retry metadata path; benchmark shows negligible latency increase but fixes routing correctness.
workaround: Add connection-level duplicate pin header (X-Model-Pin-Static) at customer-side or increase prewarm sizes for pinned variant. Support provided instructions and verified mitigation for NexusContent.
